## Purpose

In MoRI-IO WRITE (push) mode, decode requests can get stuck in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` forever when decode is overloaded. The engine stays healthy and keeps serving new requests, so this shows up as a benchmark that never finishes rather than as an error. At 1024 in / 1024 out, 128 requests at concurrency 64, with decode limited to 20 running requests, runs on `main` stall before all requests finish.

This PR fixes two causes. A third cause, decode preemption, is fixed by #53250. This PR used to include the same change, but it has been removed in favour of that PR.

### 1. Prefill gives up on a deferred write without telling decode

In push mode the proxy sends each request to prefill and decode at the same time. Prefill computes the KV cache and then waits for decode to allocate blocks and send their IDs. If decode is busy, the request can wait in decode's queue for longer than `defer_timeout` (60 s). On `main`, prefill then frees its blocks and drops the write, but never tells decode. When decode later admits the request, it waits for KV that will never arrive.

Now, when a deferred write times out:

- Prefill marks the transfer as finished under the lock, so a late block allocation from decode is ignored and no write can start. If the allocation arrived just before the timeout, the write goes ahead as normal.
- Prefill sends `write_failed` to every decode DP rank. Prefill never received the allocation, so it cannot know which rank owns the request. Ranks that do not own it ignore the message, and decode keeps only a bounded number of unmatched failures.
- Prefill then releases its blocks, even if sending a notification failed. This is safe because no write was ever issued.
- Decode reports the request as a failed KV load. It is then failed or recomputed according to `kv_load_failure_policy`. Because no write was issued, decode can free its blocks straight away.

The prefill scheduler no longer has its own WRITE-mode timeout that freed blocks on its own. Only the worker releases them, after the transfer is marked finished.

### 2. A full local prefix-cache hit sent an empty block list

When decode already had the whole prompt in its prefix cache, it sent prefill an empty block list. Prefill rejects that with `MoRIIOError("block_notify_list cannot be empty")` and keeps its blocks. Decode now sends a release message instead, so prefill frees them.

### Related PRs

- #53250 stops a preempted decode request from waiting for a second push. Under the overload above, decode preemption also strands requests, so this PR relies on #53250 to fully fix the hang. With `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`, #53250 is also what lets a failed request recompute locally.
- #58962 adds a receive timeout on decode for when prefill dies mid-transfer. In that case decode cannot know whether a write is still in flight, so it keeps the blocks. The two PRs cover different failures: this one handles a live prefill that never started the write, and #58962 handles a prefill that cannot send anything.


## Test Result

All 207 MoRI-IO unit tests pass on ROCm with `mori` installed (204 on `main`, plus 3 new). The new tests, in the CPU-only `test_moriio_write_done_routing.py`, cover:

- an expired deferred write: the transfer is marked finished, prefill blocks are released, `write_failed` reaches every decode DP rank across pods, and a late allocation is ignored
- the prefill scheduler waiting for the worker's ACK instead of freeing WRITE blocks on its own timeout
- decode reporting `write_failed` as a failed KV load on the rank that owns the request

End-to-end, using the commands above with #53250 applied (2× Radeon AI Pro R9700S, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), the benchmark finishes and KV cache usage returns to zero on both prefill and decode:

| decode `kv_load_failure_policy` | Successful | Failed | Deferred writes timed out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fail` (default) | 109 | 19 | 19 |
| `recompute` | 128 | 0 | 34 |

This is a necessary upstream fix for the unconditional async-load decision, empty block notification, and deferred-write timeout behavior.

The `do_remote_prefill` gate and full-local-prefix-hit release look correct. One concern remains: `_process_deferred_tasks()` now keeps deferred writes indefinitely by resetting `enqueue_time`, while the scheduler can still expire `_deferred_send_deadlines` and release the producer blocks after the same configured timeout.
  A late remote allocation could then execute a stale write after its source blocks have already been released or reused.

Could we either address this lifecycle mismatch in this PR or split out the deferred-timeout change? The worker task should be marked terminal before its source blocks are released, ideally with an explicit failure signal to the consumer.

Addressed in `a87a3e8`.

The WRITE timeout lifecycle is now:
1. Re-check remote allocation under the wrapper lock (an allocation racing the timeout wins and proceeds normally).
2. Mark the transfer terminal.
3. Send a structured `write_failed` notification to decode.
4. Only after that notification succeeds, ACK the producer scheduler so source blocks can be released.

Decode reports the notification through the existing `KVConnectorTransferResults.failed_recving` path, which releases `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and uses the configured failure policy (recompute by default). The scheduler-side deadline no longer independently reaps WRITE transfers; READ keeps its existing watchdog.

I also added regression coverage for terminal-before-release ordering, the allocation/timeout race, rejecting a late allocation, failure propagation, and ensuring WRITE is not scheduler-reaped. Focused/adjacent MoRI-IO tests pass (46 total), pre-commit passes, and the normal GPU WRITE path completes 64/64 with no engine errors.

Thanks for the review, @simondanielsson. I've pushed fbc4b2928, which addresses your comments:

- I removed the `do_remote_prefill` change, since #53250 makes the same fix.
- `write_failed` is now sent to every decode DP rank, as you suggested in your inline comment.

On the timeout fix not being fully reliable: you're right that a message can always be lost if decode crashes. But the bug this PR fixes is not caused by a lost message. When decode is overloaded, it can admit a request more than `defer_timeout` after prefill finished. Decode then sends its block IDs late, not never. On `main`, prefill has already dropped the write and freed its blocks by then, and it never tells decode. So decode waits forever even though no message was lost.

`write_failed` uses the same ZMQ connection as the block IDs and `write_done`, so it is no less reliable than the messages push mode already depends on.

I also think this fix and #58962 are both needed, because they handle different failures:

- **This PR:** prefill is alive but timed out before it started writing. Prefill knows no write was issued, so decode can free its blocks immediately and fail or recompute the request.
- **#58962:** prefill died or lost its connection mid-transfer. Decode cannot know whether a write is still on its way, so it has to keep the blocks.

With only #58962, an overloaded decode would fail these requests after its own timeout but keep their blocks until restart, even though nothing will ever write to them. If `write_failed` is ever lost, #58962's timeout still fails the request.

I've also updated the PR description to match. Note that this PR now relies on #53250: under the same load, decode preemption still leaves requests stuck until that PR lands.

A note on scope: I found a separate, pre-existing issue that this PR deliberately leaves alone. It does not apply the per-pod host and local-rank handling that the `remote_blocks` notify uses. On a Wide-EP multi-pod deployment, a release for a prefill rank on a child pod can therefore go to the wrong host and port, and prefill holds those blocks until its deferred-write timeout. Independent validation at `cf61c55c` on a P3D1 overload workload

I hit the cause-1 hang in a disaggregated benchmark before finding this PR. I built this branch from source and tested it on the same workload. It fixes the hang.

**Setup**
- Build: PR head `cf61c55c` (base `9d2a6f52`), built from source for gfx942. AITER v0.1.23, FlyDSL 0.3.4.1, torch 2.13, Triton 3.7.1, amd_mori 1.2.3.post1, ROCm 10.0.
- Hardware and topology: one MI300X split into 4 QPX/NPS1 partitions, 3 prefill + 1 decode (TP1, EP).
- Connector: MoRI-IO WRITE over xGMI, `kv_load_failure_policy=fail`, prefix caching off, CUDA graphs on.
- Model and load: Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8. Synthetic summarization, 8192 input / 512 output tokens, concurrency 128, 1280 requests (aiperf 0.12.0).
- With only one decode partition, decode fits about 17 of these requests at a time, so prefilled requests queue on decode.

#53250 isn't merged yet, so both builds include it, since this PR relies on it. The only difference between them is this PR. "Before" is `9d2a6f52` + #53250. "After" is `9d2a6f52` + #53250 + this PR.

| Build | `defer_timeout` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| before | 15 | Hung 44 s into the run: decode at `Running: 0, Waiting: 128, Deferred: 17`, KV usage 95.1%, after 129 "Deferred write task ... expired". No progress for 20 min, then I stopped it. |
| after | 15 | Finished in 410 s. 409 completed, 871 failed. Decode KV at 0% at the end. |
| after | 60 (default) | Finished in 1029 s. 1280/1280 completed, 636 output tok/s. Decode KV at 0% at the end. |

- I set `defer_timeout=15` so that requests reliably wait on decode longer than the timeout, which triggers the bug. At the default 60 the same hang happened on v0.28.0 too, but only after about 4 minutes and not on every run, so 15 gives a repeatable comparison.
- At 15 s with this PR, prefill timed out 872 writes. One was aiperf's readiness probe: decode had already rejected it with HTTP 400, and prefill timed it out 15 s later. The other 871 are exactly the 871 requests the client saw fail. No request was left waiting and no decode KV leaked.
- The 60 s run had no timeouts apart from the probe. It shows nothing regressed; it does not exercise the fix.
- Unit tests: `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio*.py` at `cf61c55c`, 207 passed.

**Not tested:**
- `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`
- TP>1, DP>1 and multi-pod setups
- RDMA

**Side observation**, not about this PR: with `fail`, failed requests reached the client as an empty response through the toy proxy rather than an HTTP error.

detail.body:
## Purpose

In MoRI-IO WRITE (push) mode, decode requests can get stuck in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` forever when decode is overloaded. The engine stays healthy and keeps serving new requests, so this shows up as a benchmark that never finishes rather than as an error. At 1024 in / 1024 out, 128 requests at concurrency 64, with decode limited to 20 running requests, runs on `main` stall before all requests finish.

This PR fixes two causes. A third cause, decode preemption, is fixed by #53250. This PR used to include the same change, but it has been removed in favour of that PR.

### 1. Prefill gives up on a deferred write without telling decode

In push mode the proxy sends each request to prefill and decode at the same time. Prefill computes the KV cache and then waits for decode to allocate blocks and send their IDs. If decode is busy, the request can wait in decode's queue for longer than `defer_timeout` (60 s). On `main`, prefill then frees its blocks and drops the write, but never tells decode. When decode later admits the request, it waits for KV that will never arrive.

Now, when a deferred write times out:

- Prefill marks the transfer as finished under the lock, so a late block allocation from decode is ignored and no write can start. If the allocation arrived just before the timeout, the write goes ahead as normal.
- Prefill sends `write_failed` to every decode DP rank. Prefill never received the allocation, so it cannot know which rank owns the request. Ranks that do not own it ignore the message, and decode keeps only a bounded number of unmatched failures.
- Prefill then releases its blocks, even if sending a notification failed. This is safe because no write was ever issued.
- Decode reports the request as a failed KV load. It is then failed or recomputed according to `kv_load_failure_policy`. Because no write was issued, decode can free its blocks straight away.

The prefill scheduler no longer has its own WRITE-mode timeout that freed blocks on its own. Only the worker releases them, after the transfer is marked finished.

### 2. A full local prefix-cache hit sent an empty block list

When decode already had the whole prompt in its prefix cache, it sent prefill an empty block list. Prefill rejects that with `MoRIIOError("block_notify_list cannot be empty")` and keeps its blocks. Decode now sends a release message instead, so prefill frees them.

### Related PRs

- #53250 stops a preempted decode request from waiting for a second push. Under the overload above, decode preemption also strands requests, so this PR relies on #53250 to fully fix the hang. With `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`, #53250 is also what lets a failed request recompute locally.
- #58962 adds a receive timeout on decode for when prefill dies mid-transfer. In that case decode cannot know whether a write is still in flight, so it keeps the blocks. The two PRs cover different failures: this one handles a live prefill that never started the write, and #58962 handles a prefill that cannot send anything.

## Test Plan

Unit tests, which need neither ROCm nor the `mori` package:

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_write_done_routing.py
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio*.py
```

End-to-end reproduction in WRITE mode with the `xgmi` backend. Start the proxy first so both engines can register:

```bash
python examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 8402
```

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --port 8400 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_producer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "xgmi",
      "read_mode": false,
      "proxy_ip": "127.0.0.1",
      "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
      "http_port": "8400",
      "handshake_port": "8600",
      "notify_port": "8500"
    }
  }'
```

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --port 8401 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 20 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "xgmi",
      "read_mode": false,
      "proxy_ip": "127.0.0.1",
      "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
      "http_port": "8401",
      "handshake_port": "8601",
      "notify_port": "8501"
    }
  }'
```

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://localhost:8402 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 8088 --ignore-eos
```

`--max-num-seqs 20` makes decode the bottleneck so that some requests wait longer than `defer_timeout`. Add `"kv_load_failure_policy": "recompute"` to the decode config to have timed-out requests recomputed instead of failed.

## Test Result

All 207 MoRI-IO unit tests pass on ROCm with `mori` installed (204 on `main`, plus 3 new). The new tests, in the CPU-only `test_moriio_write_done_routing.py`, cover:

- an expired deferred write: the transfer is marked finished, prefill blocks are released, `write_failed` reaches every decode DP rank across pods, and a late allocation is ignored
- the prefill scheduler waiting for the worker's ACK instead of freeing WRITE blocks on its own timeout
- decode reporting `write_failed` as a failed KV load on the rank that owns the request

End-to-end, using the commands above with #53250 applied (2× Radeon AI Pro R9700S, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), the benchmark finishes and KV cache usage returns to zero on both prefill and decode:

| decode `kv_load_failure_policy` | Successful | Failed | Deferred writes timed out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fail` (default) | 109 | 19 | 19 |
| `recompute` | 128 | 0 | 34 |

This is a necessary upstream fix for the unconditional async-load decision, empty block notification, and deferred-write timeout behavior.

The `do_remote_prefill` gate and full-local-prefix-hit release look correct. One concern remains: `_process_deferred_tasks()` now keeps deferred writes indefinitely by resetting `enqueue_time`, while the scheduler can still expire `_deferred_send_deadlines` and release the producer blocks after the same configured timeout.
  A late remote allocation could then execute a stale write after its source blocks have already been released or reused.

Could we either address this lifecycle mismatch in this PR or split out the deferred-timeout change? The worker task should be marked terminal before its source blocks are released, ideally with an explicit failure signal to the consumer.

Addressed in `a87a3e8`.

The WRITE timeout lifecycle is now:
1. Re-check remote allocation under the wrapper lock (an allocation racing the timeout wins and proceeds normally).
2. Mark the transfer terminal.
3. Send a structured `write_failed` notification to decode.
4. Only after that notification succeeds, ACK the producer scheduler so source blocks can be released.

Decode reports the notification through the existing `KVConnectorTransferResults.failed_recving` path, which releases `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and uses the configured failure policy (recompute by default). The scheduler-side deadline no longer independently reaps WRITE transfers; READ keeps its existing watchdog.

I also added regression coverage for terminal-before-release ordering, the allocation/timeout race, rejecting a late allocation, failure propagation, and ensuring WRITE is not scheduler-reaped. Focused/adjacent MoRI-IO tests pass (46 total), pre-commit passes, and the normal GPU WRITE path completes 64/64 with no engine errors.

Thanks for the review, @simondanielsson. I've pushed fbc4b2928, which addresses your comments:

- I removed the `do_remote_prefill` change, since #53250 makes the same fix.
- `write_failed` is now sent to every decode DP rank, as you suggested in your inline comment.

On the timeout fix not being fully reliable: you're right that a message can always be lost if decode crashes. But the bug this PR fixes is not caused by a lost message. When decode is overloaded, it can admit a request more than `defer_timeout` after prefill finished. Decode then sends its block IDs late, not never. On `main`, prefill has already dropped the write and freed its blocks by then, and it never tells decode. So decode waits forever even though no message was lost.

`write_failed` uses the same ZMQ connection as the block IDs and `write_done`, so it is no less reliable than the messages push mode already depends on.

I also think this fix and #58962 are both needed, because they handle different failures:

- **This PR:** prefill is alive but timed out before it started writing. Prefill knows no write was issued, so decode can free its blocks immediately and fail or recompute the request.
- **#58962:** prefill died or lost its connection mid-transfer. Decode cannot know whether a write is still on its way, so it has to keep the blocks.

With only #58962, an overloaded decode would fail these requests after its own timeout but keep their blocks until restart, even though nothing will ever write to them. If `write_failed` is ever lost, #58962's timeout still fails the request.

I've also updated the PR description to match. Note that this PR now relies on #53250: under the same load, decode preemption still leaves requests stuck until that PR lands.

1. A deferred write times out on prefill. The transfer is marked terminal, its blocks are released, `write_failed` reaches every decode DP rank across pods, and a late allocation is ignored.

I updated the description with these results.

A note on scope: I found a separate, pre-existing issue that this PR deliberately leaves alone. On `main`, `_release_write_prefill_blocks` computes the release port from the global `remote_dp_rank` and always uses `remote_host`. It does not apply the per-pod host and local-rank handling that the `remote_blocks` notify uses. On a Wide-EP multi-pod deployment, a release for a prefill rank on a child pod can therefore go to the wrong host and port, and prefill holds those blocks until its deferred-write timeout. This PR now routes the full-prefix-hit case through the same helper, so that case shares the limitation. I would rather fix it in a follow-up with its own test than widen this PR.

On the three parts:
1. **Suggestion**: This change is also implemented in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53250, can we remove it from here to avoid duplication?
2. Makes sense to me
3. **Thought**: Do I understand it correctly that the issue is if the message sent from D->P containing `remote_blocks` is lost or not sent within 60s, and hence P never writes nor notifies D that it finished writing leading to D being stuck in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` indefinitely. I think in principle it makes sense to notify D that P never received this initial message. My only reservation against this is that this solution is neither 100% waterproof as this "I never got the remote blocks"-notification itself can get lost by the same means.

For part 3 I wonder if we should rather adopt one of the following solutions:
1. retransmit the `send_notify_blocks` from D->P so the message is not randomly lost 
2. Simply fail the request on D after a timeout: basically https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58962

Happy to hear your thoughts.
